BENGALURU(SCCH-26), PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award dated 07.02.2022 passed by XXIV Additional Small Cuases Judge and the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and ACMM (SCCH-26) at Bengaluru (for short 'the tribunal') in MVC.No.2144/2018.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal and ACMM (SCCH-26) at Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation awarded by the tribunal.
Hence, the appellant seeks enhancement of compensation.
2. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.
Brief facts of the case are as under;
That on 05.03.2018 at about 8.00 p.m, the claimant was travelling on Motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-42-K-8878 as a pillion rider.

When they reached near Yakkuli village, Kodihalli hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, Ramanagara District, at that time driver of the Lorry bearing registration No.KA-42-8644 came in a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and swerved to the extreme right side of the road and dashed against the Motorcycle.

Due to which the claimant fell down and sustained grievous injuries and shifted to Sanjay Gandhi Hospital wherein he took treatment as inpatient and underwent operation, open reduction internal fixation and took rest for six months.
In view of the injuries suffered and disability sustained, the claimant filed claim petition seeking compensation against the respondents.

2 3.1.

sentences.text: On service of notice, respondent Nos.1 and 2 filed statement of objections denied the claim of the claimant including age, avocation, and income and denied the negligence attributed against the driver of the Lorry and sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

Respondent No.2 took up a plea NC: 2024:KHC:15811 that his vehicle was insured with respondent No.1, and any liability fastened on him would have to be indemnified by respondent No.1-Insurance Company.

Whereas,
respondent No.1 took up the plea that respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation, as the driver of Lorry did not possess a valid and effective Driving License as on the date of occurrence of accident, thereby committed breach of terms and conditions of the policy.
3.2. On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration.
3.3. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimants got examined himself as PW.1 and Doctor as PW.2 and another one as PW.3 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P11.

On the other hand, respondents got examined as RW.1 to RW.3 and got marked documents as Exs.R1 to R4.
3.4.

On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned counsel for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of NC: 2024:KHC:15811 Rs.2,46,000/- with interest @ 9% p.a. and directed respondent No.1-Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount and liberty to recover the same from respondent No.2-owner of the offending vehicle -Lorry within 60 days.
3.5.
Being aggrieved by the meagre compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court seeking compensation.

4. The main contention of the learned counsel for appellant-claimant is that, the tribunal has committed an error in awarding meagre compensation, which calls for interference at the hands of this Court.
Accordingly, he seeks enhancement of compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent-Insurance Company submits that the tribunal has rightly awarded just and reasonable compensation, which does not call for interference.

Therefore,
on these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.
6. Having heard learned counsel for the appellant and learned counsel for the respondent - Insurance Company, perused the impugned judgment and award.

On careful NC: 2024:KHC:15811 perusal of Exs.P1 to P6 are the police records depict the filing of FIR and charge sheet having been laid against the driver of the Lorry which is not questioned or challenged.
Hence, negligence is rightly attributed against the driver of the offending Lorry.
7. Now coming to the aspect of age, avocation, income, disability and appropriate multiplier for awarding compensation.

It is seen that the claimant was aged 33 years as on the date of occurrence of accident, the appropriate multiplier is '16', which is correctly applied by the tribunal and does not call for interference.

sentences.text: Doctor has been examined as PW.2, who has opined the disability to an extent of 30% permanent disability for upper limb, but he has not opined the disability to the limb and whole body separately.

Hence, tribunal not accepting the opinion expressed by the Doctor, assessed the disability to be 7%
as against 30%.
The tribunal has taken the income at Rs.12,500/- p.m, which is correct as per the Notional Income Chart, same does not call for interference.
9. Learned counsel for the appellant contends that the claimant was a mason by profession.
In view of the injuries NC: 2024:KHC:15811 sustained on the right hand, he is unable to do any work as a mason, which was his employable status prior to the occurrence of accident.
Though the Doctor has stated disability of 30% to the whole body, this Court is of the opinion that disability assessed by the tribunal is on the lower side.
Considering the fact that claimant was a mason, now not in a position to do any work because of his injuries suffered to the right hand, the disability could be taken at 15%.
Same is objected by learned counsel for the respondent-Insurance Company.
Therefore, loss of future income due to disability would be Rs.3,60,000/- (Rs.12,500/- x 12 x 16 x 15%) as against Rs.1,68,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
10. Towards pain and suffering, the tribunal awarded Rs.10,000/-.
This Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.
11. Towards loss of amenities, tribunal awarded Rs.10,000/-.
This Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.50,000/- under this head.
12. Towards medical expenses, tribunal awarded Rs.17,264/-.
Same is retained.
Towards food, nourishment and attendant charges, tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/-.
This Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.27,000/- as the claimant was inpatient for 27 days.
14. Towards loss of income during laid up period, the tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/-.
The claimant would require at-least four months period to recuperate and to get back to his normal day to day activities.
Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to Rs.50,000/- (Rs.12,500 x 4) under this head.
15. In view of the above discussions, the claimant would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.5,54,264/- as against Rs.2,46,000/- as mentioned in the table below:

Head Amount in Rs.
Loss of future income 3,60,000-00 Pain and suffering 50,000-00 Loss of Amenities 50,000-00 Loss of income during laid up 50,000-00 period Food, conveyance and 27,000-00 attendant charges Medical expenses 17,264-00
